## [2026-10-23](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-23.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31563>)

AOPD weights teacher guidance by whether the suggested action helps the current student succeed, rather than treating every teacher-preferred token as beneficial. An estimator built from rewarded student rollouts improves several tested math and coding distillation results without extra teacher rollouts or a learned value model, although it requires outcome rewards and does not win every benchmark.

**Published:** 2026-10-22 · **First seen:** 2026-10-23T10:02:55.075Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** On-Policy Distillation, Advantage Weighting, Outcome Rewards

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.31563v1>) · [Code](<https://github.com/Helloworld10011/AOPD>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Pinned v1 full 22-page PDF and HTML, method Section 3, experiments Section 4 and Tables 1–4, policy-space analysis Section 5 and relevant proof, setup, sampling, group-size, clipping and implementation appendices inspected. The objective favors teacher actions with positive advantage under student continuations. A change-of-measure estimator combines a sampled teacher/student probability ratio and a dense teacher expectation with a leave-one-out terminal-reward baseline from the same response group. It does not require explicit teacher-action continuation rollouts. Ratio clipping at c=4 caps the teacher measure in both terms without renormalizing it, estimating a modified clipped objective rather than preserving exact unbiasedness for the original unclipped objective. Main comparisons use LoRA rank 64, batch size 32 and non-thinking Qwen models. External math distills Qwen3-4B-Instruct into Qwen3-1.7B for 450 updates; external coding uses a Qwen3-8B teacher and 350 updates. Table 1 reports AIME24 pass@1 of 35.0% versus 32.6% for the strongest listed alternative on that metric, OPD with reverse KL, and AMC 65.1% versus 61.8%. This is not uniform dominance: HMMT is 15.8% versus 16.0% for forward-KL OPD, and other coding metrics also favor alternatives. Self-distillation conditions the same base student on a reference solution; Qwen3-8B reaches AIME24 52.1% versus 41.7% for OPSD in Table 2. Tables 3–4 include mixed domain/model outcomes, including a Qwen3-4B biology regression. Paper reward-improvement results concern exact, sufficiently small KL-proximal policy-space updates under their assumptions, not arbitrary finite-sample neural SGD. The verified author repository and pinned first substantive/current READMEs disclose a residual correction beyond the paper clipped objective and an optional forward-KL term only for all-zero-reward groups; external math uses mu=0.08. Those release additions and paper/source setting differences must not be erased in a reproduction. Original arXiv receipt October 22 17:05:21 UTC retained; original paper announcement is in the October 23 batch. Repository creation October 13 does not establish an earlier method release: the inspected complete 154-commit history starts with a LICENSE-only October 21 23:21:44 UTC commit, followed by substantive README/code from October 21 23:27:24 onward, within the 72-hour lookback. Commit dates do not prove the precise moment a repository became public. This is conservatively newly-discovered catch-up first inspected today, without claiming an indexing delay or resetting the method age to its paper announcement.

**Limitations:** AOPD requires terminal outcome rewards and teacher probabilities on student prefixes; unlike pure distillation it is not reward-free. No extra reward evaluations means reuse of already-rewarded RL rollouts, not zero scoring cost versus OPD. Main comparisons have method-specific sampling/tuning and different response-group sizes for some RL baselines, so equal update counts do not establish matched total compute or rollout budgets. No broad independent-training-seed uncertainty study is reported for the main benchmark comparisons. Results vary by task, model and metric, with explicit regressions; no general superiority to every teacher/distillation/RL baseline is established. Clipping modifies the objective, and the exact proximal theoretical guarantee does not directly cover the released residual correction or practical LoRA updates. Repository READMEs document differences between paper-default launchers and retained experiment-source settings. No training code was executed and no independent reproduction was performed.

## [2026-10-21](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-21.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Capable Teacher, Myopic Scorer: Reward-Free Teacher Repair for Agentic On-Policy Distillation](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28586>)

Rollout-to-Scorer Distillation first repairs a teacher’s token scores using its own continuations from difficult student states, then freezes that teacher for ordinary on-policy distillation. The tested agents complete more tasks and spend fewer turns on unproductive searching, showing why a teacher’s ability to solve a task can differ from the usefulness of its next-token supervision.

**Published:** 2026-10-20 · **First seen:** 2026-10-21T10:02:45.791Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Agentic Distillation, Teacher Repair, Long-Horizon Learning

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.28586v1>) · [Code](<https://github.com/Tree-Shu-Zhao/miles-agent>) · [Project](<https://tree-shu-zhao.github.io/r2s/>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Pinned v1 Sections3–5 and relevant mining, selection, training and evaluation appendices inspected. R2S mines high-disagreement states from an untrained student, generates eight teacher takeovers per state, selects short validated endings, and trains a teacher copy to reproduce takeover-conditioned Top16 token targets on the student’s complete assistant suffix without seeing the takeover. A frozen repaired scorer then supplies the standard OPD signal. Table2 covers two teachers, four students and three replayable text environments, with12 teacher-student-environment cells; the author-reported mean improvement over the best of three comparison OPD methods is12.8 success percentage points. Each main cell is one150-step training run evaluated with three decoding seeds, not three independent training seeds. The Qwen3.5-9B→4B dynamics study separately repeats student training three times while sharing one repaired teacher. Main reward-free filtering uses consensus and/or a judge; ScienceWorld completion messages and other observable end states still supply feedback. The paper is in the original October21 CL new-submission batch; original October20 receipt is retained. Author code, project and moving-main/release-tag guidance were inspected. Earlier code history is acknowledged; no exact first-public Git timestamp is inferred. Conservative catch-up classification preserves the earlier implementation context inside the72-hour lookback instead of claiming the paper batch is the first-ever public method release.

**Limitations:** Repair adds untrained-student mining, up to19,200 teacher-takeover episodes, selection and one full teacher fine-tune before the matched150 student steps, so main accuracy comparisons are not end-to-end compute matched. Most main results have only one training run per cell. Evidence is confined to Qwen3/Qwen3.5 and replayable ALFWorld/WebShop/ScienceWorld with fixed demonstrations and turn limits. Reward-free means no numeric task reward is read in selected variants, not absence of outcome cues, consensus assumptions or a model judge. A poorly aligned teacher or unreliable filter may still mislead. The capability/scoring diagnosis is evidence for these settings, not a proof that all OPD failures share one cause. No independent reproduction.

### [A Stronger Teacher Within: Strengthening MoE Models via On-Policy Bidirectional Distillation](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23185>)

MoEvolve temporarily activates more experts, repairs their cooperation by distilling from the original model, strengthens the expanded model with verifiable-reward training, and distills its gains back into the original expert budget. Across four tested mixture-of-experts backbones, this produces stronger domain-specific models without increasing their final activation budget, offering a way to improve a model using its own latent capacity instead of an external stronger teacher.

## [2026-10-16](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-16.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21337>)

STOPD randomly truncates student rollouts at block boundaries and reweights retained token losses to preserve the expected full-rollout gradient sum. Across tested Qwen students and mathematics, coding and instruction-following tasks, the authors report similar accuracy with 25-48% fewer generated tokens and 1.3-2.2x faster training steps, offering a practical way to reduce distillation cost.

**Published:** 2026-10-15 · **First seen:** 2026-10-17T10:05:55.063Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** On-Policy Distillation, Rollout Truncation, Importance Weighting

**Public availability:** 2026-10-16T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.LG/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21337>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 3-5 and relevant Appendices A/B/D-H were inspected. STOPD samples independent cutoffs, rounds each to a block end, and uses exact inverse inclusion probabilities with K=128 after 25 Vanilla warmup steps. The main comparison distills Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 into Qwen3-1.7B-Base over 250 steps, three training seeds and batch 256 on two H100s: reported full-step times are 941 to 513 seconds for math, 566 to 260 for code, and 104 to 80 for instruction following, including generation, teacher scoring, updates and other overhead. Vanilla versus STOPD endpoint aggregate accuracy is 30.1 versus 29.4 for math, 28.5 versus 28.1 for code, and 59.8 versus 60.1 for instruction following. Additional 30B-A3B-teacher experiments use 4B/8B students on two H200/GB200 GPUs respectively. Public availability is inferred as October 16 00:00 UTC from the verified cs.LG new-submission batch and official schedule; the original October 15 06:22:08 UTC receipt date is retained.

**Limitations:** The expected unnormalized gradient and token-count sums are preserved only under budget-invariant generation, prefix-local loss, independent truncation and exact inclusion probabilities. The actual normalized loss uses the previous batch token-count estimate and can retain a scale mismatch; optimizer bounds compare one step from identical parameters and state, not complete training trajectories. Evidence covers Qwen 1.7B-8B students and 250-step runs, with speed depending on rollout length, hardware and scheduling. The weight-free random-truncation ablation also preserves accuracy closely, while inverse weighting better aligns response lengths, so accuracy alone does not prove the weights necessary. No author implementation or model artifact URL was verified; cited Muon code is not a STOPD release.

### [Stochastic Teacher Intervention for Agentic On-Policy Distillation](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10878>)

STI-OPD uses teacher–student disagreement to probabilistically replace a proposed agent turn before execution, then importance-weights supervision on teacher-generated tokens. This offers a training recipe for limiting compounding trajectory errors while leaving the student to act alone at evaluation time.

### [Divergence controls entropy in distillation](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03529>)

This study separates the distillation loss from the source of sampled prefixes and finds that token-level reverse KL, rather than on-policy sampling itself, primarily drives lower entropy in its experiments. Theory and controlled language-model studies show how divergence choice, teacher updates, and probability-tail handling affect diversity, providing practical knobs for diagnosing entropy collapse during distillation.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [On-Policy Distillation](<https://thinkingmachines.ai/blog/on-policy-distillation/>)

On-policy distillation lets a student generate its own trajectories and uses teacher token probabilities to provide dense feedback on the states the student actually visits. The report demonstrates a practical route to improving reasoning and restoring instruction-following after domain training without rebuilding an entire reinforcement-learning reward pipeline.

**Positioning:** open-reference

**Evidence:** technical-report; full-text. The author report supplies reverse-KL pseudocode, reasoning and personalization experiments, and a linked implementation; its June 2026 note documents replacement models in the maintained recipe.

**Limitations:** Teacher quality and token-probability access are prerequisites; some cost comparisons use extrapolated supervised baselines, and the cookbook's replacement models do not themselves reproduce the original numerical results.
